text:
The Ducks open a three-game road trip in Vancouver after a 6-3 win over Ottawa on Sunday, a game they won after trailing by three, with Cutter Gauthier scoring three goals. They're 2-2-1 in their last five and are missing A.J. Greer and Ryan Poehling. The Canucks have lost four of five, most recently 4-2 to Toronto, and are without Filip Chytil. Elias Pettersson has moved up beside Lekkerimäki and Boeser in his absence. These teams met last week, and Vancouver won 6-5 in overtime, a game our numbers say it deserved 80% of the time.

Neither team has controlled play at five on five: Anaheim has taken 44% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and Vancouver 40%. Our model expects 3.56 goals for the Ducks and 2.93 for the Canucks. Anaheim takes 4.8 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, projected starters Lukas Dostal and Leevi Meriläinen are both close to even in goals saved above expected this season (+0.3 and +0.8), though Meriläinen sat at -17.9 last season and Dostal at -3.7.

Gauthier has a 44% chance to score by our numbers and 70% for a point, riding a four-game point streak. Leo Carlsson is at 80% for a point. For Vancouver, Filip Hronek is one point from 300 career points, and Jeff Paterson of Rink Wide posted that he's on pace for 63 points. Our under-the-radar picks are Ducks depth forward Judd Caulfield, whose shots have produced 3.2 expected goals in his last 10 games, and Mikael Granlund, at 64% for a point against a defense that gives up the second-most chances per 60. They're players to watch, nothing more.
